## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet. The starting network scored 0.000 on dev with both seeds, so for now I will rank candidates by mean training success and the training signals. The default recipe gives about 131k steps at 4,096 per update, which is only about 32 PPO updates. That looks too few for a credit-assignment problem with episodes of up to 33 steps. The starting network also has weaknesses. Its receptive field is only 5×5. Global context reaches only the DONE and value heads, so placement logits cannot see global progress such as which layer is complete. Its output logits use default init, not near-uniform init. Following the suggested split, this round tests (a) recipe only: more and smaller updates, 2 epochs, higher gamma and lambda; (b) architecture only: a deeper residual network with global pooled context fed back into every cell, footprint-shaped conv heads and small-init outputs; (c) both together.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. The failures were neither check failures nor timeouts. Every run finished in 53–76 s, so the 900 s limit leaves plenty of room. Since training success is also 0, the problem is learning itself, not generalisation. An exact build needs every placement to be correct. Placement reward is dense, and even without the +1 bonus, DONE beats adding extra cells once the build is complete. So placement accuracy, not DONE, looks like the bottleneck. The starting net mixes all layers in its first 1×1 layer, so it has to relearn the same rule (where a brick lands and whether that layer is missing cells) separately for each height. Two changes to test: (1) share weights across layers, giving each layer a 2D slice of the build, target, missing and extra cells, the build cells just below and above it, and its height, then combine layers with a learned gate that picks the landing layer; (2) many more samples from 1 PPO epoch. Neither change has a score yet, so the choices follow the reasoning above.

### Round 3
All six trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That covers the starting net, a residual net with global context, and a layer-shared net, trained with 1, 2 or 4 PPO epochs. Since training success is also 0, the problem is learning itself, not generalisation. Neither more samples alone nor these inductive biases fixed it. Two untested factors are left. First, gradient steps and policy updates: r2c2 used about 400k samples but only 52 large updates, which is about 830 gradient steps, fewer than the default recipe takes. Second, the head's ability to combine footprint-pooled features nonlinearly with global context. That combination is how it would infer the landing layer and whether a placement is correct, and how it would decide DONE. Gamma has been at most 0.98. A higher gamma makes continuing to build worth more than an early DONE. This round tests both factors: (1) many small updates on the starting net, (2) a deeper, context-conditioned footprint head, and (3) the two combined.

### Round 4
I ran 9 trials. All 9 scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, so seed noise can't explain the result. Changing only the recipe (1–2 PPO epochs, up to 400k steps, gamma 0.97–0.99, entropy 0.005–0.01) did not help. Changing only the architecture (global context, a deeper head, sharing weights across layers) did not help either. Because nothing learns at all, I suspect a structural problem rather than slow learning. I have two guesses. (1) The world may not match its description. Every network so far ties each cell's logit to the matching anchor cell through convolutions. If the action indexing or brick orientation differs from what is stated, convolutions cannot learn the mapping. A flat head can learn any mapping. (2) A random placement probably gives a negative reward, and DONE costs nothing. The policy may learn to stop at once, before it learns accurate placements. Slowing the DONE logit's learning would test this. This round tests each idea alone, both on the starting network with r1c1's recipe, and the two combined.
